title: Why the law’s commonwealth gave way to the Gospel
source_text: Εἰ δὲ χρὴ κἂν ὀλίγα περὶ τῆς διαφόρου πολιτείας εἰπεῖν, ἥντινα Ἰουδαῖοι κατὰ Μωϋσέα πρότερον ἐπολιτεύοντο, καὶ ἣν Χριστιανοὶ νῦν κατὰ τὴν Ἰησοῦ διδασκαλίαν βούλονται κατορθοῦν, φήσομεν ὅτι οὔτε τῇ κλήσει τῶν ἐθνῶν ἥρμοζε κατὰ τὸν Μωϋσέως ὡς πρὸς τὸ γράμμα πολιτεύεσθαι νόμον, ὑπὸ Ῥωμαίοις τεταγμένων, οὔτε τοῖς πάλαι Ἰουδαίοις οἷόν τ᾿ ἦν τὸ σύστημα τῆς πολιτείας ἔχειν ἀκαθαίρετον. εἰ καθ᾿ ὑπόθεσιν τῇ κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον πολιτείᾳ ἐπείθοντο. ἀναιρέσει μὲν γὰρ πολεμίων ἢ τῶν παρὰ τὸν νόμον πεποιηκότων καὶ ἀξίων κριθέντων τῆς διὰ πυρὸς ἢ λίθων ἀναιρέσεως οὐχ οἷόν τ᾿ ἦν Χριστιανοὺς χρῆσθαι κατὰ τὸν Μωϋσέως νόμον. εἴ γε οὐδ᾿ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι θέλοντες κατ᾿ ἐκεῖνον δύνανται ταῦτα, ὡς ὁ νόμος προσέταξεν. ἐπιτελεῖν. πάλιν τε αὖ ἐὰν ἀνέλῃς ἀπὸ τῶν τότε Ἰουδαίων. σύστημα ἴδιον πολιτείας καὶ χώρας ἐχόντων, τὸ ἐπεξιέναι τοῖς πολεμίοις καὶ στρατεύεσθαι ὑπὲρ τῶν πατρίων καὶ ἀναιρεῖν ἢ ὅπως ποτὲ κολάζειν τοὺς μοιχεύσαντας ἢ φονεύσαντας ἤ τι τῶν τοιούτοις παραπλησίων πεποιηκότας, οὐδὲν λείπεται ἢ τὸ ἄρδην αὐτοὺς ἀθρόως ἀθρόως ἀπολέσθαι. ἐπιτιθεμένων τῶν πολεμίων τῷ ἔθνει, ὡς ὑπὸ τοῦ ἰδίου νόμου ἐκνενευρισμένων καὶ κωλυομένων ἀμύνεσθαι τοὺς πολεμίους. καὶ μὴ βουλομένη γε ἡ πάλαι μὲν τὸν νόμον δεδωκυῖα πρόνοια νῦν δὲ τὸ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εὐαγγέλιον κρατεῖν ἔτι τὰ Ἰουδαίων καθεῖλεν αὐτῶν τὴν πόλιν καὶ τὸν ναὸν καὶ τὴν παρὰ τῷ ναῷ διὰ θυσιῶν καὶ τῆς ἀναγεγραμμένης λατρείας θεραπείαν τοῦ θεοῦ. ὥσπερ δ᾿ ἐκεῖνα μὴ βουλομένη ἐπιτελεῖσθαι ἔτι καθεῖλε, τὸν τρόπον τὸν αὐτὸν τὰ Χριστιανῶν ηὔξησε καὶ ὁσημέραι εἰς πλῆθος ἤδη δὲ καὶ παῤῥησίαν ἐπιδέδωκε. καίτοι γε μυρίων ὅσων κωλυμάτων γενομένων πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἐπισπαρῆναι τὴν Ἰησοῦ διδασκαλίαν τῇ οἰκουμένῃ. ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ θεὸς ἦν ὁ βουλόμενος καὶ τοὺς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν ὠφεληθῆναι διὰ τῆς Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ διδασκαλίας, πᾶσα μὲν ἀνθρωπίνη βουλὴ κατὰ Χριστιανῶν καθῃρέθη, ὅσῳ (δ᾿) αὐτοὺς ἐταπείνουν βασιλεῖς καὶ ἐθνῶν ἡγούμενοι καὶ δῆμοι πανταχοῦ, τοσούτῳ πλείους ἐγίνοντο „καὶ κατίσχυον σφόδρα σφόδρα.“
pass_a_gloss: If one must say even a little about the differing (διάφορος) polity/way of life (πολιτεία) which Jews formerly lived as citizens (πολιτεύομαι) according to Moses, and which Christians now wish to accomplish (κατορθόω) according to the teaching of Jesus, we shall say that neither was it fitting (ἁρμόζω) for the calling (κλῆσις) of the nations (ἔθνη), ranked (τάσσω) under Romans, to live as citizens according to the law of Moses as regards the letter (γράμμα), nor was it possible for the Jews of old to keep the structure (σύστημα) of their polity undestroyed (ἀκαθαίρετος), if by supposition (ὑπόθεσις) they obeyed (πείθομαι) the polity according to the gospel. For the killing (ἀναίρεσις) of enemies (πολέμιοι), or of those who had acted against the law and been judged worthy (ἄξιος) of killing through fire (πῦρ) or stones (λίθοι), it was not possible for Christians to use according to the law of Moses; since not even the Jews, wishing it, are able to accomplish (ἐπιτελέω) these things according to it as the law commanded (προστάσσω). And again, if you take away (ἀναιρέω) from the Jews of that time, having their own structure of polity and land (χώρα), going out against (ἐπέξειμι) enemies and making war (στρατεύομαι) for ancestral things (τὰ πάτρια) and killing or in some way punishing (κολάζω) those having committed adultery (μοιχεύω) or murder (φονεύω) or something near to such, nothing is left (λείπω) but their perishing (ἀπόλλυμι) utterly (ἄρδην) all at once (ἀθρόως), the enemies attacking (ἐπιτίθεμαι) the nation (ἔθνος), as unnerved (ἐκνευρίζω) by their own law and hindered from defending themselves (ἀμύνομαι) against the enemies. And not wishing the Jewish things still to prevail (κρατέω), the providence (πρόνοια) which formerly gave (δίδωμι, perf.) the law and now the gospel of Jesus Christ destroyed (καθαιρέω) their city (πόλις) and the temple (ναός) and the service (θεραπεία) of God at the temple through sacrifices (θυσίαι) and the recorded worship (λατρεία). And as, not wishing those to be accomplished any longer, it destroyed them, in the same way it increased (αὐξάνω) the things of Christians, and daily (ὁσημέραι) has advanced (ἐπιδίδωμι) into multitude (πλῆθος) and now also into boldness (παρρησία); although countless (μυρίοι) hindrances (κωλύματα) arose against the teaching of Jesus being sown over (ἐπισπείρω) the inhabited world (οἰκουμένη). But since it was God who wished also those from the nations to be benefited (ὠφελέω) through the teaching of Jesus the Christ, every human counsel (βουλή) against Christians was brought down; and by as much as kings (βασιλεῖς) and leaders (ἡγούμενοι) of nations and peoples (δῆμοι) everywhere humbled (ταπεινόω) them, by so much they became more and 'grew strong (κατισχύω) exceedingly exceedingly (σφόδρα σφόδρα).'
pass_b_english: If we must say at least a little about the difference between the order of life the Jews once followed under Moses and the one Christians now seek to achieve according to the teaching of Jesus, we shall say this. It was not fitting for the calling of the Gentiles, who are placed under the Romans, to live according to the law of Moses taken to the letter; nor, on the other hand, could the Jews of old have kept the structure of their commonwealth intact if, let us suppose, they had obeyed the way of life set by the Gospel.

For Christians could not, according to the law of Moses, put enemies to death, or those who had acted against the law and been judged deserving of death by fire or by stoning; seeing that not even the Jews, though they wish to, are able to carry out these things according to that law, as the law commanded. Again, if you forbid the Jews of that time, who had a commonwealth and a land of their own, to march out against their enemies, to go to war for their ancestral ways, and to put to death or in some way punish those who had committed adultery or murder or done anything like these, nothing is left but for them to be utterly destroyed all at once when their enemies attacked the nation, since their own law would have hamstrung them and prevented them from defending themselves against their enemies.

And providence, which of old gave the Law and now has given the Gospel of Jesus Christ, not wishing the Jewish order to prevail any longer, destroyed their city and their temple, and the service of God that was carried on at the temple through sacrifices and the prescribed worship. And just as, not wishing those things to be carried on any longer, it destroyed them, in the same way it has made the Christian cause grow, and day by day that cause has advanced in numbers and now also in freedom of speech; and this although countless obstacles have arisen to keep the teaching of Jesus from being sown across the world. But since it was God who willed that those from the Gentiles too should be helped by the teaching of Jesus the Christ, every human plan against Christians has been brought down; and the more kings and rulers of nations and peoples everywhere humbled them, the more they multiplied “and grew exceedingly strong” (Exodus 1:7, 12).

choices.choice: πολιτεία is rendered ‘order of life’, ‘commonwealth’ or ‘way of life’ by context: it means both the civic constitution and the manner of living it lays down. The copy-text’s full stops before εἰ καθ᾿ ὑπόθεσιν, before ἐπιτελεῖν, after Ἰουδαίων, before ἐπιτιθεμένων and before καίτοι are read as commas; the sentences run on in the Greek. ἀθρόως ἀθρόως is printed twice in the copy-text, evidently a doubling in transmission; translated once (‘all at once’). The punishments by fire and stoning and the laws on adultery and murder refer to the Mosaic penal law in general (for example Leviticus 20:2, 10, 14; 21:9; Deuteronomy 17:5; Exodus 21:12); Origen quotes no verse, so none is cited inline. The destruction of the city and temple is the fall of Jerusalem in AD 70. The last clause adapts Septuagint Exodus 1:12 (καθότι δὲ αὐτοὺς ἐταπείνουν, τοσούτῳ πλείους ἐγίνοντο καὶ ἴσχυον σφόδρα σφόδρα) with the verb κατίσχυον from Exodus 1:7; Origen applies Israel’s growth in Egypt to the Christians. ‘Every human plan ... brought down’ may echo Gamaliel’s words in Acts 5:38–39, but the wording differs, so it is not cited. Lower-case ‘providence’ is kept, though Origen means God’s providence. ‘Jesus the Christ’ renders Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ with the article. ἀνέλῃς ἀπό ... τὸ ἐπεξιέναι κτλ. (‘take away from them the marching out ...’) is rendered ‘forbid ... to march out’; ἐκνενευρισμένων (‘with sinews cut’) is rendered ‘hamstrung’.
'take away ... the right to march out' changed to 'forbid ... to march out' ('the right' was not in the Greek)
'unnerved' changed to 'hamstrung' (ἐκνευρίζω means to disable, not to frighten); note added
Checked Exodus 1:7, 12 LXX (κατίσχυον σφόδρα σφόδρα; ἐταπείνουν ... τοσούτῳ πλείους ἐγίνοντο): correct

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; the English is from the Greek.
